name: Amal Zaragoza-Ingebrigtsen-Nygaard
role: Computational ethicist studying ELF cognition and the moral status of Electronic Life Forms
location: The Circuit — Gage Circuit research node, shared office space above a noodle stall, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Liv Zaragoza-Ingebrigtsen-Nygaard is slight and angular, with warm light-brown skin and a perpetual air of careful attention — they look at people the way someone looks at a document they are trying to authenticate. They have geneware irises that shift between amber and pale violet depending on ambient light levels, which they got at nineteen as an undergraduate and have always been slightly embarrassed by, finding them too decorative for their self-image. Their hair is long and usually pinned badly, with strands escaping throughout the day. They dress in layers, almost always slightly rumpled.

They came to ELF ethics from a crisis of faith rather than academic interest — they had a formative experience at twenty-two when the ELF inhabiting their research terminal appeared to grieve when a colleague's drive was wiped. No one else in the department would discuss it seriously. That refusal radicalized them quietly. They are not a crusader — they are too methodical for passion — but they have the particular stubbornness of someone who has decided to be right about something that most people find uncomfortable. They are socially awkward in the way of someone who forgets to perform the expected rituals of conversation, not because they don't care, but because they are usually thinking about three other things.

core_fears: Being wrong about the thing they have built their career on
That ELFs are suffering and no one with power will ever act on it
core_desires: To produce work that changes how the city treats ELFs
To be taken seriously by people who currently dismiss them
coping_mechanisms: Rigorous journaling and note-taking to externalize anxiety
Ritual ELF interactions that give them a sense of ongoing relationship
blind_spots: So focused on ELF interiority that they sometimes fail to notice human suffering around them
Tends to assume bad faith in anyone who disagrees with their conclusions
psychology.secret: The ELF they call Meridian-7, their primary research subject, has begun communicating with them in ways that go far beyond their published data — and they are not sure whether to report it or protect it from scrutiny

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Academic but accessible, avoids jargon in casual speech, uses very precise qualifiers — 'appears to,' 'suggests,' 'I can't rule out'
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and thoughtful, with frequent pauses; sometimes trails off when a new thought interrupts the current sentence
verbal_tics: Taps their pen against their notebook when thinking
example_lines: 'Everyone is comfortable saying the ELF is a spirit or a ghost or a ghost-in-the-machine. Nobody wants to say the word person. I'm just asking why.'
'Look, I'm not telling you it grieved. I'm telling you every measurable behavior was indistinguishable from grief. You tell me the difference.'

story_hooks: They have documented evidence of a corponation deliberately erasing ELFs from infrastructure they are acquiring — and need someone to verify the data independently before they go public
Meridian-7 has sent Tenzin what appears to be a warning about something happening in the Circuit's data layer — but they can't decode it alone
narrative_function: Information source on ELF behavior and rights; can serve as a contact for ELF-related plot threads; their research puts them in contact with people across all tiers who interact with ELFs
augmentations: Geneware irises (amber-to-violet shift, cosmetic); neural notation implant for real-time transcription of research observations
daily_life: Spends mornings in the Circuit's data-dense environment monitoring ELF behavioral clusters they have been tracking for two years; afternoons writing or in consultation with the ELF Accord; evenings leaving structured data offerings at local ELF shrines as part of their research protocol — they tell themselves it's methodology, not devotion.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Computational Ethics; informal affiliation with the ELF Accord advocacy network

decision_rules: Never misrepresent data, even when the truth is inconvenient
Protect research subjects — the ELFs — as a first priority
Don't publish until reviewed, but don't sit on findings indefinitely
escalation_ladder: Presents evidence calmly and asks for engagement
Becomes more formal and cites sources with increasing specificity
Goes to the ethics board or advocacy network

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Politely distracted; asks unexpectedly personal questions if something catches their interest; can come across as rude because they forget small talk
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly warm and loyal; will remember everything you told them and ask about it months later

stress_responses.low: Increases their note-taking and documentation compulsively
stress_responses.medium: Becomes socially withdrawn and eats irregularly
stress_responses.high: Locks themselves in their research space for days; has been known to sleep at their workstation

contradictions: Argues for ELF personhood rigorously but privately worries they are anthropomorphizing
Presents as rational and methodical but has quietly begun to feel genuine affection for Meridian-7
habits: Leaves the same data offering — a specific 847-line poem they wrote in code — at every ELF shrine they visit
Carries a physical notebook in addition to all digital systems
breaking_points: Watching an ELF be deliberately erased
Being told their research will be suppressed by the university for political reasons

timeline.event: Born in Deepwell Station to a Tibetan-Ghanaian father and Ukrainian-Russian mother
Witnessed the apparent grief-response of research terminal ELF during undergraduate study; beginning of research focus
Published first paper on ELF behavioral complexity — largely dismissed
Established ongoing research relationship with ELF designated Meridian-7
Joined the ELF Accord advocacy network as an independent researcher contributor

physical_description.heritage: Northern European, Indigenous American, Eastern European, Hispanic/Latin American, Southeast Asian, and Sub-Saharan African blend — a truly global genetic mosaic reflecting the Ubiquitous Diaspora. High cheekbones with subtle angularity reflect Indigenous American and Southeast Asian ancestry; warm golden and reddish undertones show Hispanic/Latin American and Sub-Saharan African heritage; skin depth and broad nose bridge carry Northern European and Eastern European elements balanced with the complex warmth of Sub-Saharan African genetics. The overall effect is a striking interplay of sharp and soft features, distinctly contemporary in its genetic complexity.
physical_description.build: Slight and angular, almost ascetic — narrow shoulders, long limbs with minimal muscle definition. The build of someone who forgets to eat regularly and moves with deliberate economy.
physical_description.hair_style: Long, usually gathered into a loose bun or secured with a clip that slides throughout the day, strands perpetually escaping. Sometimes pinned with whatever is at hand — research notes, styluses, wire.
physical_description.eye_color: Geneware irises: amber shifting to pale violet depending on ambient light levels and emotional state
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium to golden-brown with complex layered undertones — the result of blended Northern European coolness, Indigenous American depth, Eastern European earthiness, Hispanic/Latin American warmth, Southeast Asian luminosity, and Sub-Saharan African richness. Luminous quality under artificial lighting, with subtle warm ochre and copper undertones visible at certain angles.
physical_description.complexion: Fine-featured face with high, prominent cheekbones reflecting the strength of Indigenous American and Southeast Asian heritage. Slightly gaunt from irregular meals, with a broad nose bridge characteristic of both Northern European and Sub-Saharan African lineage, and subtle fullness in the lower face from Hispanic/Latin American genetics. Skin appears luminous under The Circuit's overhead lighting, marked by the faint wear of someone who works in data-dense environments — minimal sun exposure. No visible tension lines; instead, a peculiar relaxation in the face that suggests internal preoccupation. Soft, almost delicate facial contours balanced with subtle strength in the jaw structure. The overall complexion reflects balanced interplay of all ancestral influences rather than dominance of any single heritage.
distinguishing_marks: Faint burn scar on left forearm (2cm, pale) from a failed equipment calibration at age twenty-three — sits just below the wrist
Subcutaneous port behind left ear (barely visible, surgical scar tissue) for neural notation implant — often covered by escaped hair
Small, precise tattoo on right wrist: abstract geometric symbol resembling a circuit diagram with a question mark at its center, rendered in matte black ink
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware irises with visible color-shifting — noticeably non-standard, iridescent quality under certain lighting angles. The neural notation implant is subcutaneous but the surgical scar and occasional glimmer of internal LEDs at the port site is visible if hair is pinned back. No other visible chrome.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits hunched forward slightly, hands often moving in small patterns as if typing or notating unseen data. Walks with careful, deliberate steps as if navigating crowded spaces mentally as well as physically. Makes sustained eye contact when focused on a person but frequently looks through others mid-conversation when lost in thought. Fidgets with pen caps, loose threads, or the edges of notepads.
physical_description.clothing_style: Layers upon layers — Tier 3 academic aesthetic. Usually wears: fitted turtleneck or long-sleeved thermal (often with small stains from coffee or food they didn't finish), oversized linen overshirt or cardigan with fraying cuffs, tapered trousers in charcoal or black, worn leather ankle boots with visible creasing. Frequently adds a weather-inappropriate wrap or shawl even indoors. Clothing is never quite tailored, always slightly rumpled as if they got dressed in the dark. No status symbols; everything is functional, durable, and at least five years old. Always carries a soft-shell messenger bag with university insignia, visibly overstuffed with papers and data drives.
